correctness.rationale: For d≥3, 0≤t≤2, the slab |sum x_i|≤d−t cuts exactly two disjoint corner simplices of volume t^d/d! from [-1,1]^d. The polar is conv(±e_i,±(1,…,1)/(d−t)); exactly the positive/negative cross-polytope facets are visible for 0<t<2, adding two equal pyramids of volume t/[d!(d−t)]. Hence Q_d=(1−t^d/(2^(d−1)d!))(1+t/[2^(d−1)(d−t)]). Independently verified symbolically in SymPy that derivative Q′=d/[2^(d−1)(d−t)^2]*(1−H_d(t)/d!) with H_d=t^(d−1)*[(d−t)^2+t(d−t+1)/2^(d−1)]. H′_d positive for t∈(0,2), d≥3; H_d(2)=2^(d−1)(d−2)^2+2(d−1) exceeds d! at d=3,4,5 and falls below d! at d=6, with elementary factorial induction for all larger dimensions. Thus exactly one interior optimum in d3..5 and strictly increasing Q for d≥6; independently checked exact Q_6(2)=4667/4608. Source verify.py checks rational nodes and facet signs but analytic induction supplies all dimensions. No theorem for t>2 or arbitrary convex bodies.
